A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same OCK research and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither file contains an appendix or embedded supplement; supplementary material referenced in the text is unavailable.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-prediction, scene-decomposition, long-horizon and ablation results on OBJ3D and MOVi datasets in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v3 retains original synthetic-data experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative Waymo video-prediction results in Table 3 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The encoders, analytical/empirical kinematics, Joint-OCK/Cross-OCK architectures and two-stage training remain. However, the stated reconstruction objectives change from squared norms in v1 Equations 7–8 to unsquared L2 norms in v3 Equations 5–6. This changes the written objective; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation or training runs changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluation on the Waymo Open Dataset, extending coverage from six synthetic datasets to real-world driving videos with camera motion and changing backgrounds. OBJ3D and MOVi-A through MOVi-E remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds OCVP-Seq and OCVP-Par to Table 2's scene-decomposition comparison, which previously included only G-SWM and SlotFormer. Both OCVP variants already participated in v1's video-quality comparison. The v1 table label G-SWN is corrected to G-SWM, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The added Waymo evaluation uses PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS while explicitly excluding scene decomposition because its preprocessed masks are considered unreliable. The retained MOVi training horizons, ten-frame kinematics-ablation evaluation and eighteen-frame generalization evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 4b adds a qualitative examination of predicted object trajectories using overlaid and isolated kinematics tracks. The analytical-versus-empirical comparison and input-length, transformer-depth, positional-encoding and teacher-forcing ablations are retained in Tables 4–5, corresponding to v1 Tables 3–4.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Tables contain point estimates and the generalization plots contain no uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: v3 adds Waymo results and OCVP decomposition entries. Waymo Cross-OCK reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 25.979/0.728/0.220, versus SlotFormer's 19.127/0.330/0.714. Existing OCK synthetic and ablation table scores remain unchanged. Table 1 revises MOVi-C OCVP-Seq from 19.945/0.515/0.431 to 17.945/0.415/0.631 and OCVP-Par from 19.941/0.502/0.450 to 17.941/0.402/0.650. Table 2 changes MOVi-B FG-ARI from 0.350 to 0.410 for G-SWM and 0.379 to 0.398 for SlotFormer, plus SlotFormer's MOVi-A mIoU from 0.502 to 0.505. These revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-loss definitions change mathematically from squared norms to unsquared L2 norms. The kinematics definitions and extrapolation assumption otherwise remain equivalent. The added Joint-OCK attention equation and Algorithm 1 largely formalize the previously described procedure; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: v1 claims demonstrated success in synthetic environments and presents real-world use as future potential. v3's introduction and conclusion claim effectiveness in both synthetic and real-world environments, materially broadening the demonstrated applicability of the contribution. The central kinematics-based prediction claim remains.

C2.justification: The limitations are substantially reframed. v1 explicitly acknowledges synthetic-only evaluation, two-stage-training inefficiency and unsatisfactory absolute MOVi-E decomposition performance. v3 focuses on the slot encoder's limitations in natural videos and possible replacement, dropping the latter two caveats. Its Waymo discussion adds high-speed motion, changing backgrounds and unreliable masks as difficulties. It also newly asserts robustness without rotation/scaling factors and attributes baseline divergence to inadequate slot extraction.

D1.justification: v3 specifies extracting object centers as 2D coordinates, provides procedural pseudocode in Algorithm 1, and adds OBJ3D sequence length/resolution and Waymo scene counts, native resolution and frame rate. These are documentation additions rather than evidence of changed preprocessing. Conversely, v1's explicit unit-length normalization description for Cross-OCK kinematics is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DDLP, Waymo and Bridging the Gap to Real-World Object-Centric Learning, while removing works including SCALOR, SPACE and CLEVRER. These update context and support the real-world discussion; the principal positioning relative to SlotFormer and OCVP remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively revised, with stronger emphasis on dynamic video prediction and the expressivity–accuracy tradeoff. Related-work subsections are reordered, experimental details and metrics are consolidated, ablation discussions are reorganized, and the limitations section is rewritten. These changes extend beyond inserting the new experiment.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is replaced with an architectural comparison, Figures 2–3 are redrawn, Figure 4 gains trajectory panels, and Waymo receives a new figure and table. Table 2 expands and Figure 6 is restyled. v1's per-slot montage is absent from the supplied v3, which instead references supplementary material.

improvement.justification: The Waymo experiment addresses v1's synthetic-only evidence, while the expanded decomposition comparison and clearer kinematics documentation improve assessment of the method. The net gain is limited by sparse Waymo training/evaluation details, unexplained revisions to baseline scores and loss definitions, and removal of specific efficiency and MOVi-E limitations. These tradeoffs support a modest improvement rather than a substantial validation upgrade.
